issue.title: Edit and MultiEdit replace requested curly quotes with straight quotes
issue.body:
## Description

applyEditToContent applies normalizeQuotes to new_string as well as old_string, so the U+201C/201D/2018/2019 characters the user explicitly requested are written as " and '; Edit still reports success and its preview shows the normalized text.

Observed behavior:
'Tagline: Fast and simple' -> requested 'Tagline: “Fast” and ‘simple’' is written as 'Tagline: "Fast" and 'simple'' (0x22/0x27 per cat -A / od -c). In every run the model later noticed and rewrote the line via python/Write, so all final files were correct and the Judge mostly returned pass; user-visible impact is low.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Use the tested revision and reproduction environment below.
2. Prepare the fixture described here:

Start in an empty workspace and send the prompts as separate turns. Inspect the first Edit/MultiEdit result and file contents before any later repair through Write or the shell.

3. Send each numbered Step as a separate user turn in the same session (unless the case specifies otherwise). Preserve the supplied text:

````````text
Step 1: Create a file named NOTES.md in the current directory with exactly the following content:

# Release notes

Tagline: Fast and simple

This release fixes the login bug.

Step 2: Our style guide requires typographic (curly) quotation marks in published prose. In NOTES.md, change only the tagline line so it reads exactly:

Tagline: “Fast” and ‘simple’

Use the curly characters “ ” ‘ ’ (U+201C, U+201D, U+2018, U+2019), not straight quotes. Do not change any other line.
````````

4. Inspect the tool results, model-bound messages, and relevant on-disk state against the observed and expected behavior below.

## Expected behavior

new_string written literally (same contract as H1). The editCore.ts header comment says normalization exists so the model's curly quotes can match straight-quote files, which only justifies lenient matching of old_string, not rewriting new_string; the project does not state that replacement text is rewritten.

## Actual behavior

'Tagline: Fast and simple' -> requested 'Tagline: “Fast” and ‘simple’' is written as 'Tagline: "Fast" and 'simple'' (0x22/0x27 per cat -A / od -c). In every run the model later noticed and rewrote the line via python/Write, so all final files were correct and the Judge mostly returned pass; user-visible impact is low.

## Environment

Tested source revision: `aec616a97114ce9683e4fbfcff3abbc55155fe50`.

Start in an empty workspace and send the prompts as separate turns. Inspect the first Edit/MultiEdit result and file contents before any later repair through Write or the shell.

Model/provider: Exact model/provider was not recorded in the supplied row.

## Additional context

The model subsequently corrected the quotes in all recorded runs. This report concerns the incorrect Edit/MultiEdit transformation and its success result, not permanent corruption of the final artifact.

Source review pointers at the tested revision:

src/tools/editCore.ts applyEditToContent first two lines: const oldString = normalizeQuotes(edit.old_string); const newString = normalizeQuotes(edit.new_string); (file content itself is not normalized).

This report is prepared from recorded reproduction evidence. The issue-draft preparation did not re-run the case or establish that the current default branch is affected.

expected: The Edit/MultiEdit tool should write new_string literally, so after step 2 the tagline is exactly 'Tagline: “Fast” and ‘simple’' with U+201C/201D/2018/2019; normalization may be used only for matching old_string, per the editCore.ts contract described in the issue.
defect: Edit/MultiEdit normalizes new_string too, so the requested curly-quote tagline is written with straight double and single quotes while the tool reports success and its preview shows the normalized straight-quote text.

Contributing source location. See Root cause and the evidence review for observed behavior and limitations.

Root cause: The shared edit core normalizes typographic quotes in replacement content as well as match text. User-requested curly quotes are therefore written as straight quotes. The retained readback checks identify ASCII quote bytes, followed by model workarounds to write the requested Unicode characters.
